stories.title: QB Caleb Williams, WR Rome Odunze's chemistry helps Bears stun Lions
stories.summary: QB Caleb Williams and WR Rome Odunze leaned on their chemistry trust to secure Chicago's ninth win of the season.
stories.detail: DETROIT -- The feeling late on Thanksgiving Day was familiar for Caleb Williams . Down three with the game on the line and the Chicago Bears ' first division win within reach, Williams turned his most trusted weapon to pull off a come-from-behind victory against the Detroit Lions , sending the Bears home from their trip to Ford Field with a 39-35 win . Facing third-and-goal with nine seconds remaining, Williams found Rome Odunze sprinting towards the back right corner of the end zone. The route that the former 2024 first-round picks repped with the clock winding down countless times in practice was moments from paying off when Williams zipped a pass in Odunze's direction. Using every inch of his 6-foot-3 frame, Odunze leapt up in the air to grab the ball with both hands as Lions cornerback Rock Ya-Sin attempted to push the receiver out of bounds. Odunze immediately believed his feet were in bounds, given where they landed in relation to the boundary, but his 6-yard touchdown catch was briefly reviewed before being confirmed. "Obviously the camera's going to tell," Odunze said. "The eye in the sky never lies, but they were looking if I stepped out of bounds before I caught it. So t…

stories.title: Schottenheimer defends 4th-down call before Eagles' 59-yard FG in 39-38 stunner over Cowboys
stories.summary: — Brian Schottenheimer said he second-guesses plenty of his decisions, just not the one that will be dissected more than any other in his two seasons as coach of the Dallas Cowboys.
stories.detail: ARLINGTON, Texas -- — Brian Schottenheimer said he second-guesses plenty of his decisions, just not the one that will be dissected more than any other in his two seasons as coach of the Dallas Cowboys . Jake Elliott kicked a 59-yard field with 2 seconds remaining, and the Philadelphia Eagles stunned the Cowboys by rallying for a 39-38 Thanksgiving victory on Thursday. The Eagles (4-7) got a chance for the win when Schottenheimer decided to go for it with a two-point lead on fourth-and-1 from the Philadelphia 39-yard line with 55 seconds remaining. Dak Prescott was sacked at the 48 of the Eagles, who needed just 11 yards to give Elliott a shot at the long field goal with 7 seconds to go. A punt could have run off about 10 seconds and pinned the Eagles deep in their end of the field with no timeouts. The shocking loss is sure to turn up the pressure on Schottenheimer after the Cowboys (5-7) again failed to win consecutive games and made any path to the playoffs difficult at best. “Absolutely not in that situation,” Schottenheimer said when asked if he second-guessed the decision. “There's things that come up and you look at the film and you want to know, ‘What do you think about tha…

stories.title: Brady disappointed in Rodgers' McCarthy comments: 'Nobody wins'
stories.summary: Tom Brady expressed his disappointment in how Aaron Rodgers handled his exit from Pittsburgh, saying there are things in the locker room that shouldn't be made public.
stories.detail: Tom Brady expressed his disappointment in how fellow future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers handled his benching and exit from the Pittsburgh Steelers , saying "nobody wins when the family feuds." Brady addressed the situation during the Fox broadcast of Eagles-Cowboys on Thursday, one day after Rodgers went scorched earth on Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy in a lengthy interview on "The Pat McAfee Show." "[The] NFL locker room is a very sacred place, and we shouldn't ever lose track of that as players," Brady said. "It's a privilege to be in that locker room, when you're fighting with your teammates, you're fighting with your coaches, you're always acting as a team together. It shouldn't always be the place for private things to become public, that's what I'll say." Following the news of his benching for backup Mason Rudolph , Rodgers went after McCarthy with a litany of accusations -- including that the coach has slept through team meetings -- and called into question his fitness to coach. Brady called Rodgers a "tremendous player" but said the situation he created was "unfortunate." A seven-time Super Bowl champion, Brady reflected that it's his relationships with his coaches and…

stories.title: Mike Tomlin on the Rodgers-McCarthy situation in Pittsburgh: 'It's a dumpster fire'
stories.summary: Tomlin addressed the Rodgers-McCarthy situation in an interview that aired during halftime of the Chiefs-Bills game.
stories.detail: Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin sat down with Mike Tirico to discuss his reaction to everything Aaron Rodgers said in a rant during Wednesday’s episode of the “Pat McAfee Show.” The highlight of the interview was Tomlin's response when asked about his emotions watching what is happening with the Steelers after coaching them for two decades. “I'm upset about it. It's a dumpster fire and I don't say that in a judgmental way. I've presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years, but it certainly is upsetting and I'm sure Steeler Nation is upset.” Tomlin started the interview by being asked for his general reaction to what was said. “I had a range of emotions watching those course of events yesterday. The prevailing one is general sadness. Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career in the quarterback, Aaron Rogers, and just on the macro level, whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum, those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football.” The former Steelers head coach said that he was “shocked” at how the team’s dirty laundry was aired. “It certainly did. stories.detail: Many folks in and around football have had opinions about the recent brouhaha between former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and Steelers coach Mike McCarthy. Few have the insight and perspective that former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin brings to the table. Appearing on NBC's Chiefs-Bills halftime show on Thanksgiving night, Tomlin shared his thoughts on the situation in a conversation with Mike Tirico. (A portion of it was on the live broadcast; the full interview is here .) "I had a range of emotions watching those course of events yesterday," Tomlin told Tirico. "I think the prevailing one is just general sadness. Sad on a micro level, sad on a macro level. And by that, I mean, you know, just from an individual perspective, sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career of the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, and just on the macro level, whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum. "Those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football. So, just a lot of emotions, but probably more than anything, man, general sadness on a lot of levels." stories.detail: The Philadelphia 76ers could be short-staffed when they take on the Indiana Pacers in NBA Cup play on Friday night. Center Joel Embiid is listed as questionable due to a lingering illness that has sidelined him for Philadelphia's last two games. Brown picked up the hamstring issue in Wednesday's NBA Cup win over the Miami Heat. He left the game late in the first half and did not return. The guard missed two games last week with a left hamstring strain, but returned to action against the Portland Trail Blazers and played 29 minutes. Toward the end of the first half, the Philadelphia guard reached toward his left hamstring and shook his head before checking himself out of the game. Embiid is dealing with an illness, though not much has been released about what symptoms he may be dealing with. Regardless, he has missed two consecutive games. The center was listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Heat, but was downgraded before the game. stories.title: Jaylen Brown out against Pacers; Joel Embiid (illness) questionable
stories.summary: The 76ers' Jaylen Brown (hamstring) is out for Friday's NBA Cup game against the Pacers. Joel Embiid (illness) is questionable.
stories.detail: PHILADELPHIA -- Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown (left hamstring) will miss Friday night's NBA Cup game against the Indiana Pacers . Center Joel Embiid , who has missed the last two games with an illness, is questionable. After scoring his sixth point of Wednesday night's win over the Miami Heat on a step-back jump shot late in the second quarter, Brown immediately shook his head and grabbed his hamstring then signaled to the Sixers bench that he needed to check out of the game. The injury started for Brown in last week's win over the Brooklyn Nets in which he tied his season high of 31 points. Brown left that game early because of a left hamstring strain and missed the Sixers' next two wins over the Orlando Magic and Milwaukee Bucks . He returned in Monday's loss to the Portland Trail Blazers , scoring 20 points. After that game, Brown said he had "a little bit of soreness." For the season, Brown is averaging 21.4 points, six rebounds and 3.4 assists. Friday's game is the final of NBA Cup group play. With a win, the 76ers will clinch Eastern Conference Group B and advance to the knockout rounds for the first time.

stories.detail: Disclaimer ** While this article mentions Phoenix Suns experiences, this piece is about the gratitude that comes with covering the team . stories.summary: It was a guy who didn’t play who served as a catalyst for the Knicks’ most all-around win this year.
stories.detail: Jordan Clarkson; Pacome Dadiet It was a guy who didn’t play who served as a catalyst for the Knicks’ most all-around win this year. Coach Mike Brown used 12 players in the team’s 121-102 win over the Cavs on Wednesday night at Madison Square Garden. Without OG Anunoby (calf strain) and Miles McBride (adductor tightness), it meant end-of-the-bench reserves got a rare chance to see some action. Pacôme Dadiet had seven points in 14 minutes. Rookie Tyler Nickel, making his NBA debut (he has spent this year in the G League), got nine minutes and had five points. Mohamed Diawara got four minutes and chipped in three points. James Wiseman saw six minutes of action and helped seal the win with a few crucial rebounds late — he finished with six offensive rebounds. Under Brown’s anything-goes system, nobody is too far away from getting a chance. His love of experimentation, particularly early in the year, means players seemingly out of the rotation will get their opportunity to prove themselves at some point.
